intro: Lesson 31: Excretion in plants and animals. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.a: B) Breathing out carbon dioxide. CO₂ is a waste product of respiration, made by cells.

questions.q: Which gas is a waste product of respiration?
Name the blood vessel that carries blood to the kidney.
Explain why carbon dioxide release from lungs is excretion.
questions.a: CO₂ is a waste product of respiration (1), a metabolic reaction in cells (1)
questions.model: Excretion means waste made by metabolism. Where does CO₂ come from? Respiration in cells. So it is excretion.

questions.q: Name the waste product made from excess amino acids and the organ that makes it.
Why do plants release oxygen in the day?
questions.a: Photosynthesis makes more oxygen than respiration uses

questions.q: Describe how the lungs, kidneys and skin excrete waste, and explain why faeces are not excretory products. Portal response box.
questions.a: Lungs: CO₂ (1); kidneys: urea, water, salts as urine (1); skin: sweat with water, salts, urea (1); faeces are undigested food (1), not made by metabolism, so egestion (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes 'The lungs excrete carbon dioxide, a waste product of respiration.'

questions.q: Trace urea from the liver to the bladder through named blood vessels and organs.
questions.a: Liver → hepatic vein → vena cava → heart → aorta → renal artery → kidney (1, 1); urine → ureter → bladder (1)

questions.q: Why does a plant in the dark release CO₂ but not O₂?
questions.a: No photosynthesis in the dark; respiration continues.
